title: R799--Northport EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Sharon Sirotnak
description: Northport, NY EUL Request for Expressions of Interest DRAFT PRE-DECISIONAL INTERNAL VA USE ONLY 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY VA Northport Healthcare System within Veterans Integrated Service Network 2 (VISN 2) Northport VA Medical Center (VAMC) located within Northport, NY Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the agreed upon use of the assets. VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Northport VAMC Campus under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject Campus assets in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigation activities to produce development with the underutilized assets at the Northport Campus. The assets that may be redeveloped by the Developer include, but are not limited to, one or more of the following buildings (Note: All of these buildings are currently listed on the National Register of Historic Places): 18, 23, 25, 26, 27, and 37. Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. Northport VA Medical Center Background The Northport VA Medical Center, established in 1928, is a major healthcare facility serving Veterans across Long Island, New York. Located at 79 Middleville Road in Northport, New York resting on 268 acres, it is part of the VA New York/New Jersey Health Care Network (VISN 2) and operates under the VA Northport Healthcare System, which includes two mobile clinics and community-based outpatient clinics located in Bay Shore, East Meadow, Patchogue, Riverhead, and Valley Stream. As a teaching hospital affiliated with SUNY Stony Brook, it offers a wide range of medical services from primary and specialty care to mental health, women s health, rehabilitation, and geriatric programs. Focused on Veteran-centered care, Northport VA also provides innovative Whole Health services like acupuncture, yoga, and nutrition counseling. The Campus has an onsite Emergency Department as well as residential living centers, it houses around 500 beds and plays a key role in both Veteran care and medical education in the region. Sources Sought Response Requirements VA is seeking qualified developers who have a proven company track record of: Developing projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated assets. Financial wherewithal required to successfully develop the proposed use(s) with associated amenities (if applicable); and, Securing public and private financing for projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated assets. For SDVOSB/VOSB developers, VA is seeking to confirm the Respondent s ability to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Responses should be submitted on official letterhead, must include a point of contact and the signature of at least one organization officer. Responses must address the following elements in sufficient detail to highlight the Respondent s ability to undertake the development scope as set forth in this Sources Sought Notice. Responses must not exceed 15 pages, single spaced with a minimum 12-point font. Response content should consist of the following: Business Information Please provide the following for your company: Company Name Address Point of Contact Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page URL SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Based on the NAICS Code identified in the Sources Sought, please state whether your company is: Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB)* (Yes / No) Service-Disab

RESPONSES: Responses to this notice should include company name, address, telephone number, cage code, and point of contact (POC). Do you recommend one type or perhaps a hybrid (i.e. a contract that allows several types)? Provide any general comments, thoughts, and feedback your company would like to share regarding this Sources Sought Notice. After the review of the responses to this sources sought announcement, and if the USCG still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a solicitation announcement will be published on the SAM.gov website. Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Raamovereenkomst inzake het documentmanagementsysteem Documentum (OpenText) van het provinciebestuur Vlaams-Brabant
description: Het provinciebestuur Vlaams-Brabant maakt reeds geruime tijd gebruik van het documentmanagementsysteem Documentum (OpenText) ter ondersteuning van zijn kernprocessen, waaronder dossierbeheer. Het platform vormt een belangrijke bouwsteen binnen het applicatielandschap van de provincie en ondersteunt verschillende bedrijfskritische toepassingen en gegevensverzamelingen. Om de continuïteit, beschikbaarheid en ondersteuning van deze omgeving op korte en middellange termijn te waarborgen, wenst het provinciebestuur een raamovereenkomst af te sluiten met een gespecialiseerde dienstverlener die over de nodige expertise beschikt inzake Documentum en de bijhorende technologieën. De opdracht omvat in hoofdzaak de levering en het onderhoud van de noodzakelijke softwarelicenties, abonnementen en ondersteuningsdiensten die vereist zijn om de bestaande Documentum-omgeving operationeel, ondersteund en conform de geldende voorwaarden van de fabrikant te houden. Daarnaast wenst het provinciebestuur binnen deze raamovereenkomst een beroep te kunnen doen op gespecialiseerde technische en functionele expertise voor uiteenlopende opdrachten en ondersteuningsvragen. De raamovereenkomst moet eveneens toelaten om beroep te doen op expertise in het kader van archiverings- en rationalisatietrajecten. Aangezien de concrete noodzaak, impact en bijhorende licentie- en implementatievoorwaarden momenteel nog niet volledig gekend zijn, wordt een eventuele upgrade voorzien binnen de raamovereenkomst zonder dat het provinciebestuur zich verbindt tot effectieve afname.

title: Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Raamovereenkomst i.v.m. leveren en bedrijfsklaar installeren van een Digitaal Asset Management systeem (DAM-software) voor het provinciebestuur Vlaams-Brabant
description: Eind 2022 is het provinciebestuur Vlaams-Brabant gestart met het gebruik van Kadanza, een cloudgebaseerde Digital Asset Management (DAM)-oplossing voor het centraal beheren en consulteren van digitale content en assets. Vandaag wordt deze oplossing voornamelijk gebruikt door de communicatiedienst en de dienst toerisme voor het beheer van fotomateriaal. Binnen het provinciebestuur beheren echter ook andere diensten een aanzienlijke hoeveelheid digitale content, zoals foto’s en video’s. Deze is momenteel vaak verspreid over verschillende platformen (zoals netwerkschijven, SharePoint, …), wat het beheer, de toegankelijkheid en het hergebruik bemoeilijkt. Deze content wordt bovendien niet uitsluitend gebruikt voor communicatie- en publicatiedoeleinden, maar maakt ook deel uit van interne werking en dossiervorming. Momenteel ontbreekt een uniforme en structurele aanpak voor het beheer van beeldmateriaal, inclusief de opvolging van gebruik en bewaartermijnen. Hierdoor blijft content vaak langdurig beschikbaar zonder duidelijke opvolging van relevantie of gebruik. Het provinciebestuur Vlaams-Brabant wenst daarom over te gaan tot de aankoop van een Digital Asset Management-oplossing die inzetbaar is binnen de volledige organisatie. De oplossing moet het beheer, de toegankelijkheid en het hergebruik van digital assets ondersteunen, en daarnaast toelaten om op een gestructureerde en gebruiksvriendelijke manier lifecycle-informatie (zoals metadata, statussen en bewaartermijnen) te beheren. De oplossing moet geschikt zijn voor verschillende diensten met uiteenlopende noden op vlak van beheer, toegankelijkheid, rechten en hergebruik, en moet flexibel kunnen omgaan met zowel intensief gebruik als meer ondersteunende toepassingen binnen de werking van de organisatie.

buyer: North East Scotland Regional Transport Partnership (Nestrans)
title: Transport to Employment â Utilising and Promoting the North East of Scotland Sustainable Travel Brand
description: This project is being commissioned as part of a funding award to Nestrans from a 20 million GBP Scottish Government investment during 2026/27 as part of the Tackling Child Poverty Delivery Plan, which will support measures to address the affordability, accessibility and availability barriers of transport to employment, helping to address the cost of living crisis and child poverty by saving people money in travelling to work and opening up opportunities for employment and skills training that will increase household incomes. This funding is being distributed across the seven Regional Transport Partnerships (RTPs) and the 32 Local Employability Partnerships (LEPs) across Scotland. Nestrans has received a grant award of 985,809 GBP for the 2026/27 financial year out of a total award to the RTPs of 11 million GBP. This funding will help to deliver on national strategy (Bringing Hope, Building Futures: Tackling child poverty delivery plan 2026-2031) plus regional and local strategies. Getabout is the established mechanism that Nestrans and partners use when engaging with employers and the private sector regarding transport needs and travel behaviours across the region. This can range from encouraging the use of existing sustainable travel measures or looking towards a more tailored approach with travel planning for specific workplaces. This project looks to evolve this engagement utilising the GetAbout brand, heightening impact by delivering on five distinct workstreams.

No other changes are being made to the solicitation. __________________________________________________________________________ This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for the Water Chemical Testing and Consultation Services for the Federal Correctional Complex Butner, prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. USMCFP SPRINGFIELD MEDICAL WASTE DISPOSAL: STATEMENT OF WORK Subject The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to make a single award to a responsible entity for the provision of Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. Medical Waste Disposal services shall only be used for medical hazardous waste that cannot be disposed of with garbage removed by the standard trash service. This contract is for Medical Waste Disposal that will need to be provided every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday throughout the contract. Medical Waste will primarily be Dialysis, dressing change, and sharp waste. Place of Performance Services for Medical Waste Disposal will be performed at the address 1900 W Sunshine St. Springfield, Missouri 65807. There is a commercial entrance off Sunshine Steet to access the property. The driver will proceed to the talk box and receive directions from the officer. There is a small structure that houses medical waste. Period of Performance USMCFP Springfield is soliciting for a 12-month period of performance to start date of award and end 12 months after date of award with a 6-month option to extend to 18 months after date of original award. Schedule The contractor shall pick up Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for the duration of the contract. Any deviation from this schedule will be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. There will be no pickups on federal holidays. Pickups scheduled for federal holidays will be rescheduled for the next business day. Note: Three pickups will be required each week per policy. The time of pick up will be from 7:30 am to 10:30 am or 11:30 am to 2:30 pm. Licensing Requirements The institution requires all applicable Federal, EPA, and Missouri licensing / regulations that are standard for this industry. Service must also comply with the Disposal of Patient Materials standards which I have attached below: Security Clearance Services will be provided outside the secured confines of the institution. Please see the Terms and Conditions for any further requirements. Description of Duties The objective of this contract is to provide Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. The contractor shall be responsible for, but is not limited to, the following: The contractor shall be responsible for the collection, removal, and disposal of infectious medical waste. These duties must be in accordance with all Federal, State, City ordinances, laws, and regulations. Containers to furnish will be red, reusable plastic tubs with lid with overall dimensions of not to exceed (24x24x24 inches). Preferably 31 Gallon in size tubs. Tub liners and tape will be furnished by the contractor and appropriately supplied with each pickup. The contractor will leave an appropriate number of tubs and lids to exchange upon request. This includes providing properly sanitized tubs and lids. The contractor holder will determine an appropriate quantity of tubs to have on hand. On average 8 full tubs will be picked up Monday�s and Wednesday�s. Fridays will average 16-20 full tubs. The estimated medical waste to be removed is 85,000 lbs per year. Only the actual weight of waste collected will be billed. Disposal charge does not include the weight of the reusable tubs or lids. Electronic manifest is preferred Each Invoice will contain: Date of pickup, number of pickups, total weight of waste picked up, pricing according to the contract mirroring the line items on the contract. Point of Contact Contractor shall provide a Point of Contact (POC) who shall be responsible for the delivery of the services under this contract. The POC shall have the full authority to act on behalf of the contractor on all matters relating to the daily operation of the contracted services. The contractor shall designate this individual, in writing, to the Contracting Officer (CO) prior to contract start date. An alternate may be designated; however, the contractor must identify those times when the alternate shall be the primary POC. English Language Requirements The contractor performing the services under this contractual agreement shall have the ability to read, understand, fluently speak and legibly write in the English language. Government Quality Assurance The Government reserves the right to inspect and evaluate all services provided during the performance under this contract. All observations will be documented by the designated Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). When an observation indicates defective performance, the Contracting Officer, along with the support of the COR, may issue a Discrepancy Report to the contractor. The contractor shall address any Discrepancy Report in writing to the COR and the Contracting Officer, within ten (10) calendar days of notification indicating any corrective action to be taken to rectify the deficiency. Non-Personal Services Information The service is a contractual arrangement and not a personnel appointment. Payment is based on the provision of an end product or the accomplishment of a specific result. The service does not constitute an employer/employee relationship. title: SEEK EAGLE MODELING, ANALYSIS, AND TOOLS SUPPORT (SEMATS) 4
description: THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer�s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO�s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include �inherently governmental functions� nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to �deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.� The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. Shortterm situations may make performance in excess of 8 hours per day, 40 hours per week necessary on occasion. The Contractor must ensure that they can provide for this contingency. 1.6 Tasks. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, Modeling & Simulation (M&S), analysis, and tool and/or product development support. title: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing
description: The Department of the Navy Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) / Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) hereby issues this announcement regarding a forthcoming Area of Interest (AOI) for Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicles (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing. MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. We invite interested parties with expertise in innovative solutions to complex problems, vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems, and general maritime experience to participate in this opportunity. Vendors will be evaluated on platform maturity, open-architecture autonomy compatibility, endurance, payload integration capacity, and rapid-production scalability. To meet the critical operational demand signal for high-volume autonomous vessel procurement over the next decade, DRPM RAS will employ innovative and streamlined acquisition pathways. The government will leverage the authorities of 10 U.S.C. 3458 (Commercial Solutions) and 10 U.S.C. 4022 (Other Transactions) and intends to award Basic Ordering Agreements and prototype other transaction agreements, and potentially production contracts or transactions to successful vendors. To maintain technical superiority and capture rapid commercial innovations, DRPM RAS intends to issue the AOI with a rolling open window. This open call will allow new entrants to compete and existing vendors to submit updated product blocks and modular payload configurations. Approved platforms will be accepted into the maritime marketplace hosted on drones.mil. This digital clearinghouse will empower authorized acquisition authorities and operational stakeholders across the Department of War enterprise to rapidly configure and issue funded delivery orders for vetted maritime autonomous systems without redundant procurement cycles. Formal AOI release is planned on or before September 30, 2026. Detailed AOI instructions will be released via SAM.gov and syndicated at https://drones.mil. Interested industry vendors capable of delivering commercial or dual-use maritime unmanned surface systems are encouraged to ensure active SAM.gov registrations and monitor this notice for amendments, industry day announcements, and formal AOI documentation. All inquiries concerning this notice must be submitted in writing to the Agreements Officer at Christopher.j.murr.civ@us.navy.mil (note this email is distinct/different than the auto generated SAM.gov).

title: SEEK EAGLE MODELING, ANALYSIS, AND TOOLS SUPPORT (SEMATS) 4
description: EDITED (20260730): After reviewing the extract from the draft PWS, vendors interested in responding to this sources sought announcment should send a statement of interest that broadly matches their own capabilites and already-demonstrated experience to those services shown below. While links to your company's website are appreciated, your response should not simpy refer us to your website. THE BELOW INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM THE DRAFT PWS FOR THIS FUTURE SOLICITATION. WHILE THE INFORMATIOIN IS DEEMED ACCURATE WITH REGARDS TO THE SCOPE OF WORK REQUIRED, THE USG RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE INFORMATION AND TASKS PRIOR TO THE OFFICIAL RELEASE OF THE RFP PWS. 1.0 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES 1.1 General. This is a non-personnel services contract to provide SEEK EAGLE Modeling, Analysis, and Tools Support (SEMATS) 4 services to the U.S. Air Force SEEK EAGLE Office (AFSEO). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform SEMATS 4 as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government Furnished Property and services. The contractor shall meet the standards in this contract. This includes the planning, coordination, and surveillance of the activities necessary to ensure disciplined work performance and timely resources application to accomplish all tasks under the contract. The contractor shall be responsible for maintaining communication with the contracting officer (CO) and the contracting officer�s representative (COR), and to immediately notify both the CO and the COR of any problems that would prevent timely performance of this contract. The contractor is responsible for and required to implement, and maintain management control systems necessary to plan, organize, direct, and control all activities under this contract. 1.1.2 Scope. This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes, in general, the required efforts under the SEMATS 4 Task Order (TO). The Contractor shall ensure that a broad range of expertise is available to support assigned tasks within mission responsibilities. The primary scope of the work is to provide software and data-based modeling, M&S, analysis, and tool and/or product development support. The scope includes professional engineering and technical support, management and non-technical support services for the AFSEO�s compatibility evaluation and mission planning processes and the development of M&S tools and products. The scope also encompasses network support services for an array of advanced M&S tools and high-performance computing resources as well as first line USAF Standard Desktop support. The SEMATS 4 scope does not include �inherently governmental functions� nor does it permit or include Personal Services. 1.2 Background. Air Force Pamphlet (AFPAM) 63-129, Chapter One, The SEEK EAGLE Program, defines the United States Air Force (USAF) standard process for aircraft-stores certification and designates the AFSEO as the organization responsible for managing all store certification activities. The mission of the AFSEO is to �deliver war-winning capability by expanding the compatibility of state-of-the-art stores on current and future generation aircraft, and by providing accurate combat weapon delivery software.� The AFSEO executes this mission by providing manpower, engineering tools, computer models and simulations, data, engineering rationale, and mission planning software applications necessary to safely load, carry, and employ inventory and developmental stores (e.g. weapons, tanks, pods) on fleet aircraft, along with the research and development necessary to influence follow-on aircraft and weapon system designs and production. Historically, the majority of the AFSEO mission has been focused on aircraft with externally carried weapon systems. As fifth-generation aircraft enter service and sixth-generation aircraft begin to materialize, the focus on carrying weapon systems in internal weapons bays will increase. In addition, weapon technologies continue to advance resulting in lighter weight weapons with complex geometric shapes, multiple aerodynamic surfaces, and advanced electronics. As these technologies mature and war-fighting capabilities increase, it becomes increasingly important to address aircraft-store compatibility issues. To understand the overall effects on aircraft performance and weapon employment characteristics due to advancing technology, extensive Modeling and Simulation (M&S), analyses, and test (both ground and flight), are required to assure safety-of-flight for the aircrew, weapon employment acceptability, and air worthiness. Expert skills and technological developments are needed to impact future aircraft and store designs/design changes for the purpose of providing maximum operational capability for the warfighter. The dynamic nature of the technical support requirements demands the availability of a workforce with flexibility and experience committed to accomplishing current tasks as well as the development of tools and models required to influence future aircraft weapon systems necessary to meet future challenges. The transfer of models, simulations, and tools from the aircraft original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to the AFSEO and the Contractor is essential for the research and development efforts necessary to determine solutions to future warfighter requirements. The Contractor shall be proficient in the continued research and development of these OEM products for the purpose of the investigation of possible solutions, the evaluation of solutions, and the documentation of solutions for future warfighter outcomes and capabilities. This PWS requires systems engineering, requirements analysis, design, and development of applicable models and simulations, which will integrate into higher level system elements for the purpose of producing aircraft weapon system solutions. Open air, ground and flight testing will be required to validate the model and simulation predictions required for improved warfighter capabilities. Additionally, research and development activity and products produced from the Contractor, in support of the AFSEO, influence the design, development, and manufacture of future aircraft weapon systems, as well as upgrades to fielded systems. 1.3 Inherently Governmental Function. The contractor shall not perform inherently governmental functions as defined in FAR Subpart 7.5 in relationship to this PWS. 1.4 Period of Performance. This is a five-year contract with 1 basic year and four option years. 1.5 Location and Hours of Work. Accomplishment of the effort contained in this PWS requires work at Contractor and Government facilities across various geographical locations (primarily in the continental United States (US)). The primary location of work is Eglin AFB FL. Normal workdays are Monday through Friday except US Federal Holidays. Workers normally work eight (8) hours per day, 40 hours per week. Flexible working hours (i.e. flextime) are permitted when performance is on-site, within the following guidelines: flextime workers shall not start earlier than 0600 and not later than 0900. Core hours of work are from 0900 to 1500 daily. All employees, whether working on-site or remotely, are expected to be available during core hours. title: RFB to Lease the Stow-Hardy House at Minute Man National Historical Park
description: Summary of the Opportunity This Request for Bids (RFB) provides the opportunity for interested individuals and organizations to submit bids to the National Park Service (NPS) to lease NPS property for residential use (single family) at Minute Man National Historical Park under the following general terms and conditions. See attached �Draft Lease� for complete terms of occupancy. Property Offered for Lease Stow-Hardy House The Stow-Hardy house is located at 965 Lexington Road, Concord, Massachusetts, 01742. It is approximately 2,400 Sq. Ft with 3 bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms and is situated on an approximately 0.4-acre landsite. The colonial style home was built circa 1786 and has been completely restored and renovated while retaining its original central arch chimney, oak timber framing, cedar shingle roof, and historic siding. The house has had significant mechanical upgrades including new plumbing, septic, heating, and electrical systems as well as a new smart washer and dryer. The kitchen features new stainless-steel appliances and a central island with farmhouse sink. The historic Battle Road Trail is located nearby, behind a mature Black Walnut grove. The trail is used year-round and provides the opportunity for various outdoor activities and connects the historic towns of Concord and Lexington. Uses of the Leased Property This lease is most suitable for low-impact, non-transient, residential occupancy of the house. The lessee is authorized to use the property as an occupant of the house and must be willing to become a part of the National Historical Park�s relationship with the public by maintaining the historic and well-tended appearance of the structure and grounds. In accordance with the attached draft lease, the lessee is responsible for all utilities and routine maintenance. The lessor will perform basic maintenance of the property as described in the lease. Term of Lease The lease will have a maximum term of three years. Lessee termination rights (termination without cause) will begin 90 days before the end of the first year of the lease and continue until the lease expires. Please note: 90 days� notice is required for termination without cause. Fair Market Value Rent The lessee will be required by the lease to pay at least fair market value rent to the NPS. Based on the terms included in the attached Lease (Section 5. Rent), the fair market value rent has been determined to be $51,600 annually, payable in equal monthly installments of $4,300 each month. The lessee shall pay to the United States as rent the sum of Fifty-One Thousand Six Hundred Dollars ($51,600) per year as the base rent payable to the National Park Service and forwarded by the lessee to the Superintendent, Minute Man National Historical Park. Rent checks will be mailed to Minute Man National Historical Park, 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742, attention Superintendent. The annual rent shall be paid on the 1st day of each month in advance monthly installments of Four Thousand Three Hundred Dollars ($4,300). Payment covering the first month will be submitted with the executed lease. Other Terms and Conditions None. Competitive Process This lease opportunity is open to all interested persons on a competitive basis. The bidder submitting a responsive bid offering the highest monthly rent will be selected for award of the lease (subject to a determination of financial capability and reference check). A responsive bid is a bid that meets the material terms and conditions of this request for bids (see attached lease terms). The bid must offer a rental amount that is no less than fair market value described in the Fair Market Value Rent section of this RFP. If two or more bids are equal, a drawing shall make the lease award by lot limited to the equal responsive bids received. Initial and Rolling Bid Submissions Bids must be received by the date listed on the first page of this RFB and must be submitted electronically in the format provided on the following pages. A public bid opening will occur the next day after the Initial Bid Submission Deadline. If a winning bid is not selected on that date, the NPS will open bids every following Monday at 1:00 PM until a responsive bid has been submitted or until NPS terminates the solicitation. Authority This RFB is issued under the authority of federal law and regulations. The applicable law is found in United States Code at 54 USC 1021 and leasing regulations may be found in the Code of Federal Regulations at 36 CFR Part 18. This RFB and the offered lease are subject to and incorporate all terms and conditions of Part 18 as applicable. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this RFB and Part 18, Part 18 controls. For Further Information Please Contact: Mike McCarthy Administrative Officer Minute Man National Historical Park 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742 Phone: (781) 472-0970 E-mail: mike_mccarthy@nps.gov NPS reserves the right at any time and in NPS� sole discretion, to cause or do any or all of the following: Waive or correct any defect or technical error as to form or content of this RFB or in any bid, response, proposal, or proposal procedure, as part of the RFB or any subsequent selection and negotiation process. Modify, amend, cancel, or suspend any and all aspects of the RFB and selection process. Reissue an RFB. Modify the scope of the Lease or the required responses or modify the components of the Lease. Request that Respondents clarify, supplement, or modify the information submitted. Extend deadlines for accepting RFB responses, or request amendments to responses after expiration of deadlines. Consider comparable projects owned, developed, or operated by a Respondent. The National Park Service and Minute Man National Historical Park The National Park Service and its Mission America�s National Park Service was created by Congress to �conserve the scenery and the natural and historic objects and the wildlife therein, and to provide for the enjoyment of the same in such a manner and by such means as will leave them unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations.� Additionally, the Congress has declared that the National Park System should be, �� preserved and managed for the benefit and inspiration of all the people of the United States.� The National Park Service has as its overall mission the preservation and public enjoyment of significant aspects of the nation�s natural and cultural heritage. To learn more about the National Park Service, visit our website at www.nps.gov. This site includes information about who we are, our mission, NPS policies and individual parks. Minute Man National Historical Park Minute Man National Historical Park was created by an Act of Congress on September 21, 1959 �� to preserve for the benefit of the American people certain historic structures and properties of outstanding national significance associated with the opening of the War of the American Revolution�� The specific purposes of the park include: �� the preservation of the historic landscape along the road between Lexington and Concord, (2) sites associated with the causes and consequences of the American Revolution, and (3) the Wayside on Lexington Road in Concord �.� To learn more about Minute Man NHP visit our website at: https://www.nps.gov/mima/index.htm. title: AN/ALE-47 Common Carriage Production IDIQ
description: DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. INTRODUCTION: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) at Patuxent River, MD announces its requirement to procure production-representative, flight-certified hardware to transition the AN/ALE-47 Common Carriage (CC) Countermeasures Dispensing System from the Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) phase into rate production. This modernization program replaces the legacy AN/ALE-47 round-magazine dispenser system with a modernized, square-magazine architecture. This allows the Navy to deploy standard 1"x1"x8" square expendable countermeasures, expanding aircraft magazine capacity from 30 to 48 rounds and aligning joint logistics with the USAF, US Army, and F-35 platforms. The contract will cover the manufacture, testing, and delivery of the following Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) and associated Support Equipment: SA-2669A/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Sequencer: Modernized electronic control unit with upgraded processing, firmware loading capabilities, and increased memory to support the legacy dispenser, as well as next-generation intelligent expendables. D-74/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Dispenser Housing Assembly: Ruggedized mechanical housing that mounts to the aircraft structure to secure the magazine assembly. MX-12772/ALE-47(V) Common Carriage Magazine Assembly: Upgraded high-capacity magazine capable of holding 48 individual 1"x1"x8" square expendable cartridges (a 60% capacity increase over legacy systems). AN/ALM-300 Support Equipment: Next-generation Organizational-Level (O-Level) flight line test sets. The estimated contract value will be $104,000,000.00 across United States Navy and Marine Corps. The proposed class of contracting actions will procure an estimated range of 114 - 186 shipsets per year for Fiscal Year (FY)28 through FY30 to satisfy the requirement. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible businesses capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this notice. ELIGIBILITY: The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is 5865: Electronic Countermeasures, Counter-countermeasures and Quick Reaction Capability Equipment. All interested businesses are encouraged to respond. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: This contract is planned to contain a three (3) year ordering period to satisfy requirements for FY28 through FY30. The anticipated award date is May 2028. The Government anticipates end item deliveries will commence as early as 12 months after each contract delivery order award. Initial production is anticipated to be an estimated 10 shipsets per month. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: The contract type for this effort is anticipated to be a Firm Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The legacy countermeasure dispensing systems across the Navy fleet are limited by 1980s computer processing architectures and a proprietary round-magazine design with a capacity of 30 expendables. The Common Carriage (CC) program modernizes this critical survivability suite. By upgrading to square expendable geometry, the Navy streamlines its global supply chain with joint partners and paves the way for advanced, intelligent expendables (e.g., active radio-frequency expendables). Additionally, the system increases the capacity from 30 expendables to 48 expendables. The system also modernizes sequencing, upgrading the processing power and communication datalinks. This program is transitioning out of Engineering and Manufacturing Development (EMD) and entering production to outfit fleet deployers. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: Interested sources must demonstrate qualified capability, active facilities, and certified quality controls (such as AS9100) to execute: Flight-Critical Electronic WRA Assembly & Quality Control: Demonstrated capability to manufacture, assemble, and test flight-critical electronic systems and Circuit Card Assemblies (CCAs) in accordance with a certified aerospace quality management system (AS9100 or equivalent). The vendor must demonstrate experience producing high-reliability avionics designed to withstand severe thermal, shock, and vibration operational environments. Precision Mechanical & Structural Castings: Production of thin-walled aluminum castings (D-74 Housing) and machined blocks (MX-12772 Magazine) to withstand maritime environments and carrier-landing shock. Production Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) & ATP: Execution of 100% throughput of Acceptance Test Procedures (ATP) and ESS (Random Vibration and Thermal burn-in/cycling) to isolate manufacturing defects. Firmware/Software Loading and Configuration Control: Secure loading, verification, and configuration management of Government-provided Operational Flight Programs (OFP) onto the non-volatile memory of the SA-2669A Sequencer. Supply Chain & Long-Lead Time Management: A demonstrated capability to manage and mitigate long-lead time material procurement for critical microelectronic components, with a supply chain structure that can support a 12-month post-award initial delivery schedule Counterfeit Part Prevention and Material Traceability: A documented and verifiable counterfeit part prevention and detection system compliant with DFARS 252.246.7007 and 7008. The System must ensure full material traceability for all components and critical hardware back to the original component manufacturer. Interested businesses shall demonstrate that your company currently possesses or has authorized access to the necessary technical data, or has a viable plan to obtain, generate, or otherwise secure the necessary technical data, and that it will be maintained throughout the duration of the effort being solicited. Interested businesses shall demonstrate the capability to complete the requirement within the Government�s required timeline. You may also submit information that demonstrates how you could potentially meet this requirement for future production opportunities. SUBMISSION DETAILS: Interested businesses shall submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than twelve (12) 8.5 x 11 inch pages, font no smaller than 12 point, 1.5 line spaced) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirements described herein. In addition to these requirements, interested businesses shall adhere to the following submission instructions: 1. Document Type: Microsoft Word 2. Delivery: The capability statement package shall be sent by electronic mail (email) to Elizabeth V. Lamb at elizabeth.v.lamb2.civ@us.navy.mil. 3. Response Date: Submissions must be received via email no later than 1:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on 30 October 2026. 4. No classified information shall be submitted in response to this Sources Sought. 5. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed to Elizabeth Lamb at the above email address. No phone calls will be accepted. 6. All responses shall include Sources Sought Notice name/number, Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size, Cage Code, and Points-of-Contact (POC) including name, phone number, and email address. 7. The Secure Juvenile Services shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work entitled, "Juvenile Secure SOW March 2025�. This will be an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity type contract with firm fixed unit prices for all line items.
